assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new class of quantum matter: insulating bulk with protected conducting edge or surface states, born from theory and confirmed by transport and spectroscopy. It has reshaped condensed-matter physics and materials design, and it fits my sense that quantum mechanics keeps surprising us in real materials. Its ties between calculation and measured spectra are especially convincing.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall proposal). Molenkamp's group gave the first transport observation in HgTe wells. The credited list does not include Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (whose HgTe prediction enabled that experiment) or the 3D pioneers; Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is the other natural claim. The Kane, Mele, Molenkamp trio is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of independent confirmation in many materials, band-structure calculations that agree with ARPES, and a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely to somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation between the 2D quantum spin Hall and 3D topological insulator strands is unresolved and some key theorists are not in the credited names.
I rely on memory of the history and have not independently verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials: flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle quantitatively, which is the theory-experiment link I value. The field has become a major arena for correlated-electron physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat-band magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Andrei contributed early STM and transport evidence, and others (such as Cao, Fatemi) were in the experimental team, so a three-person configuration necessarily leaves out meaningful contributors.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced across many groups and techniques, though only about eight years old. The superconducting mechanism is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet fully settled and the prize could be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit split with Andrei and early experimental co-authors is contestable.
Possible prematurity compared with older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance, then the coherent-tunnelling MgO junctions with very high ratios, underpins hard-disk read heads and MRAM. This is spin-dependent quantum tunnelling in a device with large practical impact, and it is a field I know well: first-principles theory (Butler, Mathon and others) quantitatively explained the symmetry filtering in epitaxial Fe/MgO/Fe. It follows naturally from the 2007 GMR prize.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995. Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated giant TMR in MgO junctions in 2004. The credited names omit the theorists Butler and Mathon who predicted the effect, which weakens a purely experimental trio. Miyazaki is also a strong claimant, so choosing three of four is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than 25 years of use, many independent reproductions, and a clear theoretical understanding. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Omission of Butler and Mathon theory from the credited names.
Whether the prize is judged as a physics discovery or as engineering of devices.
Choosing among Miyazaki, Moodera, Parkin and Yuasa.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the first controllable framework for treating strongly correlated electrons non-perturbatively, explaining the Mott transition and, combined with DFT (DFT+DMFT), giving quantitative predictions for real correlated materials. It is central to the computational materials theory I work in, and has become a standard tool. It has made predictions that can be compared with measured spectra.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar formulated DMFT (1992) and its mapping to an impurity problem, and Kotliar's group developed realistic DFT+DMFT. Metzner, Muller-Hartmann and Rozenberg also contributed, and Metzner is not in the credited list. The Georges, Kotliar, Vollhardt set is reasonable but leaves out a decisive early contributor.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of use, extensive benchmarking against experiment and cluster extensions. Quantitative success is uneven, with some failures in realistic materials.
uncertainties: Metzner's absence from the credited names.
Whether a method-oriented theoretical advance fits the prize criterion of a discovery or invention.
Accuracy of DFT+DMFT depends on double counting and other choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third basic class of collinear magnetic order, with compensated moments but spin-split bands and anomalous Hall-type responses, and offers a route to spintronics without stray fields. It was found by symmetry analysis and DFT calculations, which is right at the centre of my field, and was followed by spectroscopic confirmation of the spin splitting.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth formulated the classification and the spin-group framework, with theory and DFT predictions. Several experimental groups (ARPES and magnetic circular dichroism) have confirmed it, and other theorists (for example Hayami, Yuan and Zunger) made related earlier observations, so priority is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Immature relative to the others: formalised around 2019 to 2022 with experimental confirmation in MnTe, CrSb and other materials only from 2024. Interpretation is still developing, so I would wait before a prize.
uncertainties: Priority disputes with related earlier work on spin-split antiferromagnets.
Short time since experimental confirmation, and applications are not yet demonstrated.
Dependence of reported effects on sample quality and domain structure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MgB2 (39 K, conventional but two-gap superconductivity) and iron-based superconductors (the first non-cuprate high-Tc family) are discoveries of new classes of superconducting materials. Two-gap physics in MgB2 was explained quantitatively by first-principles calculations, a notable theory-experiment match. The iron pnictides gave a second platform to test unconventional pairing.
assessment.attribution: Akimitsu's group discovered MgB2 in 2001 and Hosono's group the iron-based family in 2008. These are clean experimental discoveries by identifiable groups, and a two-person prize is easy to configure. Credited names for theory (such as Mazin, Kortus) are absent.
assessment.maturity: Both are widely reproduced over twenty or more years. The pairing mechanism in iron-based materials is still unsettled, and the grouping of two distinct discoveries is a compound-discovery problem.
uncertainties: Combining two distinct discoveries, which might need separate recognition.
Unresolved pairing mechanism in iron-based materials.
Limited practical impact so far compared with the cuprates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of conductance quantization in units of 2e^2/h in ballistic point contacts made the quantum nature of electron transport visible in a simple, clean experiment, and it launched mesoscopic transport. The agreement with Landauer-Buttiker theory is quantitative and reproducible, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Two groups independently reported it in 1988: van Wees and colleagues (Delft/Philips) and Wharam, Pepper and colleagues (Cambridge). The credited three align with these two papers. Theory credit (Landauer, Buttiker) is not in the credited names and Landauer has died, so attribution looks mostly clean on the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and universally textbook, but the discovery dates from 1988 and the prize may now be seen as lower in novelty than newer candidates; it is timely only in a historical sense.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as dated relative to the recent field.
Subtlety of the 0.7 anomaly is not an issue for the prize but remains an open physics topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fractional charge and anyonic exchange statistics are a deep quantum surprise in two dimensions: particles that are neither bosons nor fermions. Leinaas and Myrheim's 1977 theory, followed by shot-noise measurement of fractional charge and the 2020 collider and interferometer experiments, is a coherent story with relevance to topological quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim made the theoretical prediction of intermediate statistics. Heiblum's group did the fractional-charge shot-noise measurement. The decisive statistical-braiding experiments are due to Fève's group and to Manfra's platform, and Wilczek, Laughlin (already awarded) and Halperin are not in the credited list, so the credit configuration is hard and a three-person limit forces exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Reasonable but not fully settled: the 2020 experiments are few and the interpretation of interferometer data is still debated, though fractional charge is well established. Somewhat early for the statistics part.
uncertainties: Limited independent replication of the braiding experiments.
Omission of Wilczek and Halperin from the credited names, and the difficulty of a three-name allocation.
Fractional charge and anyonic statistics may need separate recognition.
